requirements.title: Points on every link
requirements.rationale: One number the owner can read explains both where a link stands in the stream and when it will expire.

criteria.action: for any link it returns, carry points equal to its user's start_points plus its use_count minus the number of whole 24-hour periods between its last_used_at and the time of the request, and carry expired_at, and carry neither sticky nor archived_at
criteria.contract: every link object of the API (GET /api/v1/links, GET /api/v1/links/{id}, search results, MCP get_link) has points: integer (negative allowed) and expired_at: string | null, and has no key sticky or archived_at

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table over (use_count, time since last use) -> points: (0, 0h) -> 60; (0, 23h59m) -> 60; (0, 24h) -> 59; (10, 5 days) -> 65; (0, 61 days) -> -1; (3, 200 days) -> -137. For each: seedLinks one link, set use_count and last_used_at, r = api('GET', '/api/v1/links/' + id); assert r.json.points == expected; assert r.json.expired_at === null; assert !('sticky' in r.json) and !('archived_at' in r.json)

criteria.condition: a link is used (an open, a read, a snapshot view or an MCP open)
criteria.action: add 1 to its use_count and set its last_used_at to now, so that its points become start_points plus the new use_count
criteria.contract: the next GET /api/v1/links/{id} answers use_count one higher and points == start_points + use_count

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/links/use.test.ts, extending 'records a use and redirects to the normalised URL, by session or by token': seed a link with use_count 4 and last_used_at 30 days back; GET /api/v1/links/{id}/open; assert GET /api/v1/links/{id} has use_count 5 and points 65 with start_points 60

criteria.condition: the owner adds the address of a link the library already holds
criteria.action: set the link's last_used_at to now without changing its use_count
criteria.contract: the answer's link has last_used_at equal to the request time, use_count unchanged, and points == start_points + use_count

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/links/links.test.ts, extending 'adds and boosts in order, collapses repeats and lists the invalid inputs': seed a link with use_count 2 and last_used_at 40 days back; POST /api/v1/links with its URL; assert the link's use_count == 2 and points == 62

requirements.title: Start points and removal delay as per-user settings
requirements.rationale: How long an unused link survives is the owner's choice, within bounds that keep the rules meaningful.

criteria.condition: a user requests GET /api/v1/settings/decay
criteria.action: return the user's start_points and remove_days, the defaults being 60 and 180
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body exactly {start_points: integer, remove_days: integer}; {60, 180} for a user who never changed them

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, replacing 'are 60, 120 and 180 days for a user who never changed them': r = api('GET', '/api/v1/settings/decay', {as: signIn(...)}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json == {start_points: 60, remove_days: 180}

criteria.condition: a user requests PUT /api/v1/settings/decay with start_points and remove_days each a whole number from 7 to 3650
criteria.action: store both values for that user only, so that the points of every one of the user's links and every later evaluation use them at once
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {start_points, remove_days} equal to the request; GET /api/v1/settings/decay answers the same; another user's values are unchanged

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, extending 'are stored per user': seed a link with use_count 0 unused 8 days; PUT {start_points: 7, remove_days: 3650}; assert 200; assert GET /api/v1/links/{id} has points -1; evaluateDecay(user); assert the link is expired; assert another user's settings are {60, 180}; the bounds 7 and 3650 are accepted

criteria.condition: PUT /api/v1/settings/decay carries a start_points or remove_days that is missing, not a whole number, below 7 or above 3650
criteria.action: refuse the request and keep the stored values
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with body {"error": "invalid_threshold", "field": <the field's name>, "message": "<field> must be a whole number from 7 to 3650"}; GET /api/v1/settings/decay answers the previous values

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table over bodies {start_points absent, remove_days absent, start_points 6, remove_days 3651, start_points 7.5, start_points '60'}: r = PUT; assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error == 'invalid_threshold' and r.json.field names the bad field; assert GET answers {60, 180}

criteria.condition: the owner opens the Settings page and saves its decay section
criteria.action: show the fields 'Start points' and 'Remove after expiring (days)' with their current values, send both to PUT /api/v1/settings/decay, and show a refusal's message beside the field it names
criteria.contract: the section shows exactly two number fields; after Save a success shows 'Saved' and a 400 shows the API's message next to the named field

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx, replacing the tests of 'the decay section of the settings page': FakeApi answers GET {start_points: 60, remove_days: 180}; renderPage('/settings'); assert the two labelled fields hold 60 and 180 and no 'Archive after' field exists; change Start points to 30 and Save; assert the PUT body {start_points: 30, remove_days: 180}; FakeApi answers 400 invalid_threshold on remove_days; assert the message is shown beside 'Remove after expiring (days)'

requirements.title: Expiry by the scheduled evaluation
requirements.rationale: A link the owner no longer uses has to leave the stream on its own, or the library becomes the open tabs it replaces.

criteria.condition: the scheduled evaluation runs for a user
criteria.action: make expired, with expired_at set to the evaluation time, every link of the user whose points at that time are 0 or below, whose state is active, pending or unreachable, that is not pinned and that is in no workspace, and leave every other link's state unchanged
criteria.contract: after evaluateDecay(env, userId) each such link has state 'expired' and expired_at == the evaluation time; every other link keeps its state and expired_at

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, replacing the 'dormancy', 'stickiness' and 'archiving by decay' tables with one table over (state, use_count, days unused, pinned, in a workspace) -> state after evaluateDecay: (active, 0, 60, no, no) -> expired; (active, 0, 59, no, no) -> active; (active, 10, 65, no, no) -> expired; (active, 10, 69, no, no) -> active; (pending, 0, 60, no, no) -> expired; (unreachable, 0, 61, no, no) -> expired; (active, 0, 400, yes, no) -> active; (active, 0, 400, no, yes) -> active; (active, 7, 30 uses on 6 days, unused 70, no, no) -> expired, i.e. no stickiness. Assert expired_at == the setNow time for each expired one

criteria.condition: a link is pinned or belongs to at least one workspace
criteria.action: keep it out of expiry whatever its points, while still computing its points, which keep falling
criteria.contract: the link's state stays as it was and its points are start_points + use_count - days unused, negative allowed

criteria.condition: a link is used or re-pasted after the evaluation of its user has begun and before it commits
criteria.action: leave the link as the use or re-paste left it
criteria.contract: the link's state is 'active', expired_at is null and last_used_at is the use's time after both have finished

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, extending 'leaves a link boosted after selection as the boost left it': a link with points 0; decayHooks.afterSelect opens the link; evaluateDecay(user); assert state 'active' and expired_at null

criteria.condition: the evaluation of one user fails during the hourly run
criteria.action: change none of that user's links, keep that user's last_decay_at, evaluate the other users of the run, and evaluate that user again at the next hourly run
criteria.contract: the failing user's links keep their state and expired_at and their last_decay_at is unchanged; the other users' links are evaluated; a second runScheduled evaluates the failing user

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, extending 'leaves a user whose evaluation fails as it was and evaluates them at the next run' with links whose points are 0: decayHooks.afterSelect throws for user A; runScheduled; assert A's link active and B's link expired; clear the hook; advance less than 20 hours; runScheduled; assert A's link expired

requirements.title: Removal of expired links
requirements.rationale: An expired link that nobody brought back is deleted for good, on a date the owner can see in advance.

criteria.condition: the scheduled evaluation runs for a user
criteria.action: remove every expired link of the user that is neither pinned nor in a workspace and whose expired_at is at least remove_days before the evaluation time, deleting its uses, texts, passages, events, tags, workspace memberships and stored objects, and keep every expired link whose expired_at is less than remove_days before
criteria.contract: GET /api/v1/links/{id} answers 404 for a removed link and count() of its rows in link_uses, link_texts, link_passages, link_events, link_tags and workspace_links is 0 and its SNAPSHOTS objects are gone; a link one day short keeps state 'expired'

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, extending 'deletes a link archived remove_days ago with everything it had, and keeps one a day short' with expired links: a table over (expired_at days ago, pinned, in a workspace) -> removed: (180, no, no) -> yes; (179, no, no) -> no; (400, yes, no) -> no; (400, no, yes) -> no. For the removed one assert 404 and every related row and stored object gone

criteria.condition: an expired link is pinned or belongs to at least one workspace
criteria.action: keep it from removal while it stays pinned or in a workspace
criteria.contract: the link keeps state 'expired' and stays readable through GET /api/v1/links/{id}

criteria.action: for any link it returns, carry removal_at equal to expired_at plus the user's remove_days for an expired link and null for every other link
criteria.contract: removal_at: string | null; Date.parse(removal_at) - Date.parse(expired_at) == remove_days * 86400000 for an expired link

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: an expired link with expired_at T and remove_days 180 has removal_at T + 180 days; after PUT remove_days 30 it has T + 30 days; an active link has removal_at null

execution_paths.title: An unused link expires and the owner restores it

steps.action: adds a link through the website, and its last use is then more than start_points days back
runs the hourly evaluation, which makes the link expired with its expiry time
shows the stream without the link and the Expired page with the link and 'removed on <date>'
presses Restore on the Expired page
makes the link active with expired_at cleared and last use now
shows the link in the stream and 'Nothing has expired.' on the Expired page

setup: wrangler dev --test-scheduled with local D1, the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
one link added through the API whose last_used_at is then set 61 days back with wrangler d1 execute --local
end_state: after the scheduled run the link's state was 'expired' with removal_at 180 days after expired_at, and the stream did not list it
after Restore the link's state is 'active', expired_at is null and last_used_at is the restore time
the stream lists the link and the Expired page shows 'Nothing has expired.'
smoke.pseudocode: rewrites the test in e2e/decay.spec.ts: add the link; set last_used_at back 61 days with d1(); runScheduled(page); poll GET /api/v1/links/{id} until state 'expired'; on / expect no card for it; on /expired expect its article with 'removed on' the date; click Restore; on / expect its card; on /expired expect 'Nothing has expired.'

execution_paths.title: The stream lists a much-used link above a recently used one

steps.action: adds two links, opens the first 10 times and the second once
records each use, raising each link's points to start_points plus its use count
opens the stream after the first link's last use was moved 5 days back
lists the first link above the second, each card showing its points in its decay note
